name: Highlands 24

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a single-story residential structure set well back from the roadway, positioned near the center of a large parcel densely covered with evergreen trees and sandy soil|A paved road curves along the right edge of the image, with what appears to be a driveway connection leading from the road toward the residence through the wooded terrain|The structure has a light-colored roof with multiple roofline segments visible, and a small circular or rounded feature is visible at the front of the structure|The residence is substantially screened by tree canopy on all sides, limiting ground-level visibility of the building from the road.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front approach to the property, with a paved road curving through the foreground and dense evergreen trees covering the terrain between the road and the structure|The tree coverage is continuous and close-spaced along the frontage, significantly reducing sightlines from the road to the residence|No gate, fence, or signage is visible at the road frontage in this view.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property terrain, which rises gently and is uniformly covered with dense, closely spaced evergreen trees on sandy soil|No structures, fencing, outbuildings, or access routes are visible on the right side of the parcel from this perspective|The terrain on this side is open desert scrubland with no cleared areas or pathways apparent.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which presents as a continuous expanse of dense evergreen trees on gently undulating sandy terrain with no visible rear access route, fencing, or outbuildings|The tree density at the rear is consistent with the rest of the parcel, and no cleared staging areas or secondary structures are observable from this perspective|The residence itself is not visible from the rear oblique due to tree screening.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with the same dense evergreen tree cover on sandy desert soil observed from other perspectives|The terrain on the left side shows a slight grade change and remains fully vegetated with no visible pathways, fencing, or structures|No access points or cleared areas are observable on the left side of the parcel.

considerations: The residence is set well back from the paved road and is heavily screened on all sides by dense evergreen trees, which will limit ground-level visibility of the structure from the road and reduce the effectiveness of aerial observation. The single driveway visible in the nadir view through wooded terrain represents the only confirmed vehicle access route to the structure, and its width and surface condition cannot be fully assessed from overhead imagery. Responders should anticipate limited turnaround space near the structure and restricted sightlines throughout the approach. The dense tree coverage surrounding the building on all sides is a significant factor for any responder operation at this address.
clarifications: Does the driveway from the road to the residence accommodate large emergency vehicles such as fire apparatus, and is there a turnaround area near the structure? Are there any gates, barriers, or access controls along the driveway? Are there any secondary or emergency access routes to the property other than the single driveway visible from the road? Is there an address marker or visible signage at the road entrance to the driveway? Are there any propane tanks, fuel storage, or utility shutoffs located outside the structure?
